what_this_proves: A recurring event with a reminder is proposed from the owner's own words, read back with both, written as a validated RRULE and VALARM and read back by the same parser; the index mirrors the calendar on the clock and forgets deleted events; reminders arrive once at the owner's moment; a cancel happens only under the owner's confirm policy, through the same gate as a create. Proven against the fixture calendar; a real account is the owner's step.

found_on_the_way.valarm_summary_leak: parse_calendar handled SUMMARY anywhere inside VEVENT, so an email VALARM's SUMMARY replaced the event's title.
found_on_the_way.reschedule_rewrites_series: propose_reschedule -> writer.update PUT a single VEVENT; on a recurring event that replaces the series with one event and drops its VALARM. One occurrence of a series is now refused; a reschedule keeps the reminder.
found_on_the_way.reminder_as_duration: extract_duration_minutes read '15 dakika önce hatırlat' as a 15-minute event (and 'bir saat önce' as an hour); the clause is removed before time parsing.
found_on_the_way.reminder_after_the_event: quiet hours (23:00-07:30) would defer a 06:45 reminder to 07:30; the owner's own reminder now bypasses them without joining the urgent set.
found_on_the_way.routing_gap: 'Hafta içi her gün 9'da stand-up ekle.' and 'Her ay ilk gün kira ödemesi ekle.' reached nothing: _calendar_anchor had no recurrence anchor.
found_on_the_way.oracle_pinned_shape: Occurrence.as_dict is compared with truth.json; the new fields stay on the object, not in the dict.
